originality.rationale: The relevant 2016 Veronese root theorem covers the real-rootedness ingredient and is credited as such. The new assessed mathematical claim is the simultaneous eigenvalue-majorization order of two distinct complete concentric kernel-sampling circles for all integer kernel exponents and its strict shared design optimizer. Compared a complete published single-radius Szego orbit-frame proof, general RKHS sampling material, numeric Gram-condition design, and prior finite three-orbit Hardy determinant claim; none gives the mathematical implication from two-ring orientation to full majorization. Older unindexed equivalent treatments remain possible.
residual_risks: A historical RKHS or circular-design result could encode the two-orbit majorization under an unsearched terminology.
The key numerator real-rootedness is not novel; only its transfer to simultaneous Gram spectral design is claimed.
Available literature search and the full compared studies do not constitute independent publication-priority certification.

value.rationale: An exact universal optimal angular design minimizes convex spectral interpolation risk, trace inverse, condition number, and maximizes determinant/minimum eigenvalue throughout infinitely many n and alpha. These objectives typically compete, and the Fourier–Veronese argument explains their alignment for canonical two-circle kernel sampling; this is structural rather than an arbitrary slice or routine arithmetic gain.
